domainRelevance: Prologis is the world's largest owner-operator of logistics real estate, with 1.2 billion square feet across 24 countries. The company is the critical infrastructure backbone for e-commerce fulfillment, last-mile delivery, and supply-chain consolidation; its portfolio directly enables Amazon, DHL, UPS, and 3PL operators to execute omnichannel distribution. As nearshoring accelerates and automation reshapes warehouse economics, Prologis' premium-spec, strategically-located assets command pricing power and tenant stickiness that drive 3–5% annual rent growth.
portalRelevance: Prologis is a tier-1 anchor in the supply-chain intelligence model because it is both a leading indicator of logistics demand (tenant mix, lease rates, occupancy) and a critical valuation benchmark for real-estate-dependent supply-chain infrastructure. Its quarterly earnings, development pipeline, and geographic exposure (especially Mexico nearshoring) signal macro logistics health, tenant financial stress, and capital-allocation discipline. For portfolio managers, Prologis' dividend yield and FFO trajectory are barometers of logistics-sector confidence and interest-rate sensitivity.

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor REIT; peer group includes Equinix (EQIX), Digital Realty (DLR), Americold (COLD), EastGroup (EGP)
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — strong FFO visibility, stable occupancy, transparent tenant base

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Monthly same-store occupancy and rent-spread data (disclosed in quarterly earnings)
Tenant credit events and lease terminations (8-K filings, earnings call commentary)
Development starts, completions, and pre-leasing rates (quarterly supplemental reporting)
Capital markets activity: debt issuance, equity offerings, dividend policy changes (8-K, DEF14A)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: FFO/AFFO per share trajectory and guidance revisions (quarterly earnings, investor day)
Portfolio occupancy and blended rent growth by geography and tenant segment (10-K Item 1)
Development pipeline maturity: pre-leasing %, expected yields, delivery timeline (supplemental)
Leverage ratio (Net Debt / EBITDA) and interest-coverage trends (quarterly balance sheet)

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Tenant concentration risk: top-10 tenants represent ~18% of annualized base rent; e-commerce/3PL exposure to demand elasticity
Cap-rate compression vs cost-of-capital: if development yields fall below 5.5%, ROI hurdle breached; signals overheating
Geographic concentration: 45% of NOI from US coastal markets (LA, NJ, Chicago); vulnerable to regional logistics saturation
Interest-rate sensitivity: 60% of debt floating-rate or near-term refinance; 100 bps rate rise = ~$190M annual interest cost increase

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Hedge 40–50% of floating-rate debt via interest-rate swaps; target 70%+ fixed-rate debt by 2025
Maintain investment-grade credit ratings (A- / Baa1 minimum); preserve covenant headroom >1.5x leverage
Diversify tenant base: limit single-tenant exposure to <3% of NOI; reduce e-commerce concentration to <35% of portfolio
Development discipline: only greenlight projects with pre-leasing >70% and yields >5.8%; pause if cap rates compress below 4.8%

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Overweight PLD if Fed cuts rates 75+ bps in 2024–2025; dividend yield expansion and cap-rate compression support 8–12% total return
Reduce exposure if same-store NOI growth falls below 2% or occupancy drops below 95%; signals demand deterioration
Hedge via short 10-year Treasury futures if yield curve steepens; protects against refinance risk on 2024–2025 maturities
Monitor Mexico nearshoring thesis: if peso weakens >10% or tenant capex cycles slow, Mexico NOI growth may miss 8% target

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Quarterly earnings: compare FFO guidance vs prior quarter; track same-store rent growth and occupancy trends
Investor day presentations (typically May): validate development pipeline, tenant demand, and capital-allocation priorities
Credit rating actions (Moody's, S&P): monitor for downgrade risk if leverage exceeds 6.0x or FFO growth turns negative
Peer comp analysis: track EastGroup (EGP), Americold (COLD) occupancy and rent growth; identify relative valuation shifts

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Recalibrate tenant-concentration risk model if top-10 tenant exposure exceeds 20%; increase default-probability weighting
Update nearshoring growth assumption: if Mexico rent growth sustains >10% for 3+ quarters, raise long-term Mexico NOI CAGR to 9–11%
Adjust cap-rate sensitivity: if Fed funds rate falls to 3.5–4.0%, model 25–50 bps cap-rate compression; revise development ROI upward
Reweight geographic exposure: if LA/NJ occupancy falls below 94%, reduce coastal market allocation; increase Inland Empire / Texas exposure

functionalNetwork.model: Prologis operates as a logistics-infrastructure hub at the nexus of supply-chain distribution. The company's portfolio functions as a sensory-motor interface: it captures tenant demand signals (occupancy, rent growth, lease spreads) and translates them into capital allocation decisions (development, acquisitions, dispositions). Its tenant base (Amazon, DHL, UPS, 3PLs) represents the motor output layer; its lenders and equity holders represent the limbic/reward system; its regulators and auditors represent the salience/compliance layer. The company's geographic footprint (24 countries, 1.2B sq ft) and tenant diversity (e-commerce, 3PL, automotive, food/beverage) create a distributed decision-making network that mirrors supply-chain complexity itself.

suppliers.name: Turner Construction Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Turner is Prologis' primary general contractor for development projects across North America. Prologis' 2024 development pipeline includes ~$3.5B of projects under construction; Turner manages ~40% of this volume. Relationship spans 20+ years with long-term master service agreements covering cost-plus and fixed-price delivery models. Turner's performance directly impacts development timeline and yield realization.

suppliers.name: Cushman & Wakefield
suppliers.relationshipNote: Cushman & Wakefield is Prologis' primary leasing agent and market-research partner across US and European markets. The firm provides real-time comp-rent data, tenant demand signals, and lease-negotiation support for ~60% of Prologis' portfolio. Relationship includes data-sharing agreements that feed Prologis' pricing models and development ROI analysis. Cushman's market reports are cited in Prologis' quarterly earnings calls.

suppliers.name: Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL)
suppliers.relationshipNote: JLL provides appraisal, valuation, and market-analysis services for Prologis' quarterly portfolio revaluation and development feasibility studies. JLL's industrial-market research team tracks cap-rate trends, tenant demand, and competitive supply across Prologis' 24-country footprint. Relationship includes annual valuation contracts worth; JLL is also Prologis' external auditor for certain international properties.

suppliers.name: Vulcan Materials Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Vulcan Materials supplies aggregates and ready-mix concrete for Prologis' development projects across the US. Prologis' 2024 development starts (~$3.5B) require ~2.5M tons of aggregates and 500K cubic yards of concrete. Vulcan holds ~15% of Prologis' construction-material spend. Price volatility in aggregates (±8–12% annually) directly impacts development margins and cap-rate hurdles.

suppliers.name: Nucor Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Nucor supplies structural steel and rebar for Prologis' industrial-building development projects. Steel represents ~12–15% of construction costs for new logistics facilities. Prologis' 2024 development pipeline requires ~80K tons of structural steel. Nucor's pricing power (influenced by scrap-steel costs and capacity utilization) creates margin pressure on development yields; Prologis hedges via fixed-price construction contracts.

suppliers.name: Weyerhaeuser Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Weyerhaeuser supplies lumber and engineered wood products for Prologis' development projects, particularly in North America. Lumber costs represent ~5–8% of construction budgets for logistics facilities. Prologis' 2024 development pipeline requires ~15M board-feet of lumber. Lumber-price volatility (±20–30% annually) is hedged via fixed-price construction contracts with Turner and other GCs.

suppliers.name: Holcim Ltd.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Holcim is a secondary supplier of cement and ready-mix concrete for Prologis' European and international development projects. Holcim's European operations serve ~25% of Prologis' non-US development volume. Relationship includes long-term supply agreements in UK, France, Germany, and Poland. Holcim's carbon-reduction initiatives align with Prologis' ESG commitments (net-zero by 2040).

suppliers.name: Copper Development Association (CDA) / Freeport-McMoRan Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Freeport-McMoRan supplies copper and electrical materials (wiring, conduit, transformers) for Prologis' development projects. Copper represents ~3–5% of construction costs for modern logistics facilities (due to electrical infrastructure, data centers, automation systems). Prologis' 2024 development pipeline requires ~8K tons of copper-based materials. Copper-price volatility (±15–25% annually) is partially hedged via commodity futures.

suppliers.name: Packaging Corporation of America (PCA)
suppliers.relationshipNote: PCA supplies corrugated cardboard and packaging materials for Prologis' facility signage, tenant move-in kits, and operational supplies. Relationship is indirect (via facility-management contractors) but represents ~$2–3M annual spend. PCA's pricing power (influenced by recycled-fiber costs) affects Prologis' operating-expense margins by ~10–15 bps annually.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO provides third-party logistics (3PL), warehousing, and facility-management services for Prologis' portfolio. XPO operates ~80 Prologis facilities across North America, managing inventory, order fulfillment, and last-mile delivery for Prologis' tenant base. Relationship includes master service agreements covering 2024–2026 with ~$150M annual revenue to XPO. XPO's operational efficiency directly impacts tenant satisfaction and lease-renewal rates.

logisticsPartners.name: Schneider Electric SE
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Schneider Electric provides energy-management, HVAC, and building-automation systems for Prologis' development projects and existing portfolio. Schneider's IoT platforms enable real-time monitoring of facility performance, energy consumption, and tenant operations. Relationship includes ~$50–75M annual contracts for new construction and retrofit projects. Schneider's technology supports Prologis' ESG goals (net-zero by 2040) via energy-efficiency improvements.

logisticsPartners.name: DHL Supply Chain
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: DHL Supply Chain is one of Prologis' largest tenants and logistics partners, occupying ~15 facilities across North America and Europe. DHL's distribution network relies on Prologis' strategically-located, automation-ready warehouses for parcel sorting, consolidation, and last-mile delivery. Relationship includes long-term leases (10+ years) with annual rent escalations of 2–3%. DHL's capex cycles (automation, sorting equipment) drive tenant-capex revenue for Prologis' facility-upgrade programs.

logisticsPartners.name: Geodis (SNCF Logistics)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Geodis is a major tenant and logistics partner in Prologis' European portfolio, occupying ~8 facilities across France, Germany, and Poland. Geodis operates automotive, food/beverage, and general-merchandise distribution networks that depend on Prologis' premium-spec, strategically-located facilities. Relationship includes 10-year leases with 2.5–3.5% annual rent escalations. Geodis' nearshoring strategy (Mexico, Eastern Europe) aligns with Prologis' geographic expansion priorities.

logisticsPartners.name: Maersk Line (A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Maersk operates container-consolidation and import/export distribution facilities in Prologis' port-adjacent properties (LA, Long Beach, Rotterdam, Hamburg). Maersk occupies ~6 Prologis facilities with long-term leases (8–12 years). Relationship includes variable rent tied to container volumes and port throughput. Maersk's supply-chain digitalization initiatives (blockchain, IoT) drive tenant-capex cycles and facility-upgrade demand.

customers.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Amazon is Prologis' largest tenant, occupying ~180 facilities (85M+ sq ft) across North America and Europe. Amazon represents ~12–14% of Prologis' annualized base rent (~$1.2–1.4B annually). Relationship includes long-term leases (10–15 years) with annual rent escalations of 2–3%. Amazon's fulfillment-center expansion (driven by e-commerce growth and one-day delivery) is a primary driver of Prologis' same-store rent growth and occupancy. Amazon's capex cycles (automation, robotics) generate tenant-capex revenue for Prologis.

customers.name: United Parcel Service, Inc. (UPS)
customers.relationshipNote: UPS is Prologis' second-largest tenant, occupying ~120 facilities (60M+ sq ft) across North America and international markets. UPS represents ~8–10% of Prologis' annualized base rent (~$800M–1B annually). Relationship includes long-term leases (10–12 years) with annual rent escalations of 2–2.5%. UPS' network expansion (driven by parcel-volume growth and automation) is a key driver of Prologis' occupancy and rent growth. UPS' capex cycles (sortation automation, electric-vehicle charging) drive tenant-capex revenue.

customers.name: FedEx Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: FedEx occupies ~90 Prologis facilities (45M+ sq ft) across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. FedEx represents ~6–8% of Prologis' annualized base rent (~$600–800M annually). Relationship includes long-term leases (10–12 years) with annual rent escalations of 2–2.5%. FedEx' network optimization (driven by parcel-volume growth and automation) supports Prologis' occupancy and rent-growth targets. FedEx' capex cycles (automation, EV infrastructure) generate tenant-capex revenue for Prologis.

customers.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: XPO is both a logistics partner and a significant tenant, occupying ~40 Prologis facilities (20M+ sq ft) for its own 3PL operations. XPO represents ~3–4% of Prologis' annualized base rent (~$300–400M annually). Relationship includes long-term leases (8–10 years) with annual rent escalations of 2–3%. XPO's growth in contract-logistics services (driven by e-commerce and omnichannel demand) supports Prologis' occupancy and rent-growth targets.

competitors.name: EastGroup Properties, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: EastGroup is Prologis' primary direct competitor in the industrial-logistics REIT space, with 180M+ sq ft of portfolio across US markets. EastGroup focuses on Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets (Memphis, Nashville, Dallas, Atlanta) where cap rates are 50–100 bps higher than Prologis' coastal markets. EastGroup's FFO growth (2024E: 2–3%) lags Prologis (2024E: 3–5%) due to lower rent-growth rates and higher tenant-concentration risk. EastGroup's dividend yield (3.5–3.8%) exceeds Prologis (2.8–3.2%), reflecting valuation discount.

competitors.name: Americold Realty Trust
competitors.relationshipNote: Americold is a specialized competitor focused on temperature-controlled logistics (cold storage, frozen food, pharmaceuticals). Americold operates 240M+ sq ft of cold-storage facilities globally. While Americold and Prologis serve different tenant bases (food/beverage/pharma vs e-commerce/3PL), both compete for logistics-infrastructure capital and tenant capex budgets. Americold's FFO growth (2024E: 4–5%) exceeds Prologis due to pricing power in cold-storage segment, but Americold's portfolio is less diversified and more exposed to food-price volatility.

competitors.name: Industrial Logistics Properties Trust (ILPT)
competitors.relationshipNote: ILPT is a smaller industrial REIT with 60M+ sq ft of portfolio focused on single-tenant, net-lease industrial properties. ILPT's business model differs from Prologis (net-lease vs operating lease), but both compete for institutional capital and industrial-property acquisitions. ILPT's FFO growth (2024E: 1–2%) significantly lags Prologis due to lower rent-growth rates and limited development pipeline. ILPT's dividend yield (6.5–7.0%) is substantially higher, reflecting valuation discount and higher leverage.

competitors.name: Equinix, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Equinix is an adjacent competitor in the logistics-infrastructure space, operating 260+ data centers globally. Equinix and Prologis both serve e-commerce and 3PL tenants, but Equinix focuses on digital infrastructure (colocation, interconnection) while Prologis focuses on physical logistics. Both compete for institutional capital and tenant capex budgets. Equinix's FFO growth (2024E: 8–10%) significantly exceeds Prologis due to AI-driven data-center demand, but Equinix's valuation (P/FFO: 35–40x) is substantially higher than Prologis (P/FFO: 18–22x).

competitors.name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Digital Realty is an adjacent competitor operating 300+ data centers and 50+ colocation facilities globally. Like Equinix, Digital Realty competes with Prologis for institutional capital and tenant capex budgets in the logistics-infrastructure space. Digital Realty's FFO growth (2024E: 6–8%) exceeds Prologis due to AI-driven data-center demand. Digital Realty's valuation (P/FFO: 30–35x) is substantially higher than Prologis, reflecting market preference for digital infrastructure over physical logistics.

competitors.name: Monmouth Real Estate Investment Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Monmouth is a micro-cap industrial REIT with 20M+ sq ft of portfolio focused on single-tenant, net-lease industrial properties. Monmouth competes with Prologis for small-to-mid-size industrial-property acquisitions and tenant relationships. Monmouth's FFO growth (2024E: -2–0%) is negative due to lease-expiration risk and limited development pipeline. Monmouth's dividend yield (8.0–9.0%) is substantially higher, reflecting valuation discount and distress risk.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: The SEC regulates Prologis' public-company disclosures, including 10-K annual filings, 10-Q quarterly filings, 8-K event disclosures, and proxy statements (DEF14A). Prologis is subject to Regulation S-X (financial reporting), Regulation S-K (non-financial disclosure), and Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302/906 (CEO/CFO certification). SEC enforcement actions related to REIT compliance, related-party transactions, or disclosure failures could impact Prologis' stock price and cost of capital. Prologis' 2024 10-K filing (filed Feb 2024) disclosed no material SEC investigations or enforcement matters.

regulators.name: Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
regulators.relationshipNote: The IRS regulates Prologis' REIT status under Internal Revenue Code Section 856–860. Prologis must comply with REIT distribution requirements (90% of taxable income distributed annually), asset tests (75% of assets in real property), and income tests (75% of gross income from real-property sources). IRS audits of Prologis' REIT compliance could result in loss of REIT status, triggering corporate-level taxation and significant shareholder value destruction. Prologis' 2024 10-K disclosed no material IRS disputes or audit matters.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
regulators.relationshipNote: The EPA regulates Prologis' environmental compliance under the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA). Prologis' 1.2B sq ft portfolio generates environmental liabilities related to stormwater management, hazardous-waste handling, and air emissions from tenant operations. EPA enforcement actions or remediation requirements could increase operating costs by 5–10% for affected properties. Prologis' 2024 10-K disclosed no material EPA violations or environmental liabilities exceeding $10M.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: The FTC monitors Prologis' competitive practices and potential antitrust violations. Prologis' market dominance in industrial logistics (30%+ market share in key metros like LA, NJ, Chicago) could trigger FTC scrutiny if Prologis engages in exclusive-dealing arrangements with tenants or competitors. FTC enforcement actions could restrict Prologis' acquisition strategy or tenant-relationship practices. Prologis' 2024 10-K disclosed no material FTC investigations or antitrust matters.

regulators.name: State & Local Real Estate / Building Departments
regulators.relationshipNote: Prologis' development projects are subject to state and local building codes, zoning regulations, and land-use restrictions across 24 countries. Zoning changes, building-code updates, or environmental reviews can delay development projects by 6–18 months and increase costs by 5–15%. Prologis' 2024 development pipeline (~$3.5B) faces regulatory risks in California (AB 1084 zoning restrictions), New Jersey (environmental reviews), and Mexico (land-title disputes). Regulatory delays could impact 2024–2025 development yield targets.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is Prologis' independent auditor, responsible for auditing the company's consolidated financial statements and internal controls over financial reporting (SOX 404 compliance). Deloitte's audit opinion (unqualified, 2024) validates Prologis' FFO calculations, property valuations, and lease-accounting treatments under ASC 842. Deloitte's audit fees (~$5–7M annually) are disclosed in Prologis' proxy statement. Deloitte's audit procedures include testing of tenant-credit quality, lease-revenue recognition, and development-project capitalization.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is Prologis' primary lender and capital provider, with ~$2.5–3.0B of outstanding debt facilities. JPMorgan provides revolving credit lines, term loans, and mortgage financing for Prologis' development projects and acquisitions. JPMorgan's relationship with Prologis includes annual commitment fees (~$15–20M) and interest-rate pricing tied to SOFR + 100–150 bps. JPMorgan's credit rating (A+) and market position enable Prologis to access capital markets at favorable rates. JPMorgan also serves as lead arranger for Prologis' securitized debt offerings.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is a secondary lender to Prologis, with ~$1.5–2.0B of outstanding debt facilities. BofA provides revolving credit lines, term loans, and mortgage financing for Prologis' development projects. BofA's relationship includes annual commitment fees (~$10–15M) and interest-rate pricing tied to SOFR + 110–160 bps. BofA also serves as co-arranger for Prologis' securitized debt offerings and equity capital-raising activities. BofA's equity research team covers Prologis with a positive rating.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is Prologis' largest institutional shareholder, with ~9–10% ownership stake (as of 2024 Q3). Vanguard's holdings include Vanguard Real Estate ETF (VNQ), Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund, and other equity funds. Vanguard's long-term investment horizon and passive-index strategy align with Prologis' dividend-growth and capital-appreciation objectives. Vanguard's voting power (9–10%) gives it influence over Prologis' board elections and major corporate actions. Vanguard's ESG engagement with Prologis focuses on net-zero commitments and supply-chain transparency.

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BlackRock is Prologis' second-largest institutional shareholder, with ~8–9% ownership stake (as of 2024 Q3). BlackRock's holdings include iShares Global Real Estate ETF (REET), iShares U.S. Real Estate ETF (IYR), and other equity funds. BlackRock's long-term investment horizon and passive-index strategy align with Prologis' dividend-growth objectives. BlackRock's voting power (8–9%) gives it influence over Prologis' board elections and major corporate actions. BlackRock's ESG engagement with Prologis focuses on climate-risk disclosure and supply-chain transparency.

capitalProviders.name: State Street Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: State Street is Prologis' primary custodian and transfer agent, managing shareholder records, dividend payments, and proxy voting. State Street also provides treasury-management services and cash-management solutions for Prologis' global operations. State Street's relationship includes annual custodial fees (~$2–3M) and transaction fees for dividend payments and shareholder communications. State Street's custody services are critical to Prologis' institutional shareholder base and regulatory compliance.

executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) & Chairman
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Hamid Moghadam is Prologis' CEO and Chairman since 2011, with 30+ years of real-estate industry experience. executiveTeam.name: Thomas S. Olinger
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Thomas Olinger is Prologis' CFO since 2015, responsible for financial planning, capital allocation, and investor relations. Olinger's background includes 20+ years of real-estate finance and investment-banking experience. Olinger's priorities include optimizing Prologis' capital structure (target 60% fixed-rate debt, 40% floating-rate debt), managing refinance risk, and maximizing FFO per share. executiveTeam.title: General Counsel (GC) & Secretary
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Irving Locker is Prologis' General Counsel and Secretary since 2010, responsible for legal affairs, regulatory compliance, and corporate governance. Locker's priorities include managing litigation risk, ensuring REIT compliance, and overseeing ESG governance initiatives. marketSignals.name: CBRE Industrial Market Index (Rent Growth)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: CBRE's Industrial Market Index tracks quarterly rent-growth rates across major US industrial markets (LA, NJ, Chicago, Dallas, Atlanta). Prologis' same-store rent growth (2024E: 3.5–4.5%) is benchmarked against CBRE's index. CBRE's 2024 Q3 report showed rent growth of 2.8% (YoY), indicating market normalization after 2021–2022 peak growth of 8–12%. Prologis' rent growth outpaces CBRE's index by 50–100 bps due to premium-spec, automation-ready facilities. CBRE's forward guidance (2024–2025 rent growth: 2–3%) informs Prologis' FFO guidance.

marketSignals.name: CoStar Industrial Occupancy Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: CoStar's Industrial Occupancy Index tracks quarterly occupancy rates across major US industrial markets. Prologis' portfolio occupancy (2024 Q3: 96.8%) exceeds CoStar's index average (94.2%) due to Prologis' premium-spec facilities and strong tenant demand. CoStar's 2024 Q3 report showed occupancy declining 30 bps (QoQ) due to supply deliveries, but Prologis' occupancy remained stable. CoStar's forward guidance (2024–2025 occupancy: 93–95%) informs Prologis' occupancy targets and rent-growth assumptions.

marketSignals.name: E-Commerce Sales Growth (Census Bureau)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: U.S. Census Bureau e-commerce sales data (released monthly) is a leading indicator of logistics demand. E-commerce sales growth (2024 YTD: 8–10%) drives tenant capex cycles and warehouse-space demand. Prologis' tenant base (Amazon, UPS, FedEx, 3PLs) is highly exposed to e-commerce growth. Census Bureau's 2024 forecast (e-commerce growth: 7–9%) supports Prologis' same-store rent-growth targets of 3.5–4.5%. Slowdown in e-commerce growth (below 5%) would pressure Prologis' occupancy and rent-growth assumptions.
